thread.title: Apple Stock Is 'Still Not That Cheap,' Says Analyst

title: Apple Stock Is 'Still Not That Cheap,' Says Analyst
text:
Beleaguered Apple Stock Is ‘Still Not That Cheap,’ Says Analyst By Updated Jan. 18, 2019 2:08 p.m. ET Order Reprints Photograph by William Hook Text size
Given how much bad news— and skepticism —about Apple (AAPL) has circulated in 2019, one might be surprised that the shares are still about flat so far this year.
That’s happened as fiscal first-quarter (ended Dec. 29) and full-year earnings-per-share estimates have come down about 10% and 9%, respectively, over the same period. That might look like a show of support. But during a time when the S&P 500 has risen more than 5%, it’s hard to take it that way.
Apple’s stock was recently trading at about $157, up 1%. Meantime, investors are preparing for Apple’s Q1 report, which is scheduled for Jan. 29 after the market’s close. Factset’s average EPS estimate, using generally accepted accounting principles, is $4.17, on sales of $84 billion.
Canaccord Genuity analyst T. Michael Walkley on Thursday reiterated a Buy rating and $190 price target on the stock–just ahead of Factset’s $180 average–while boosting calendar year 2019 and 2020 EPS estimates to levels that are just above, and just below, consensus, respectively. “With higher-margin services and Other Products revenue expected to grow faster than the overall company, our reduced iPhone unit sales revisions are partially offset,” he wrote Thursday.
Longbow Research’s Shawn Harrison has a Neutral rating on the stock and Q1 revenue and EPS estimates that are in line with consensus.
“Uncertainty into when iPhone demand bottoms will be an anchor even as non-iPhone growth was a positive for fiscal Q1, as was continued capital return,” Harrison wrote. “In addition, while absolute valuation has contracted, Apple is still trading essentially in-line with its 5-year average discount (20%) to the S&P 500.”
Bernstein analyst Toni Sacconaghi wrote Friday that investors have lately wondered whether another risk–that the makers of popular software products, such as Netflix (NFLX) or “Fortnite” maker Epic Games might seek to flee the App store as part of a broader move that could endanger a valuable source of high-margin revenue–could be the “next shoe to drop.”
Sacconaghi, who has a Market Perform rating and a $160 price target on Apple stock, thinks that that isn’t a risk, though he has other concerns about the company.
“We ourselves remain worried about the iPhone,” he wrote Friday. “This cycle has clearly been weak . Estimates have come down, but perhaps they still need to come down more. Apple has gotten cheaper, but it’s still not that cheap.”
Corrections & Amplifications
This story was first published on Jan. 19, 2019. It has been updated to correct the misstatement that Shawn Harrison changed his fiscal 2019 iPhone production estimates in his Jan. 18, 2019, report on Apple.
